newsitem.title: USA: FULL TEXT- GE Q2 rises 14 pct to $0.66 shr.
newsitem.headline: FULL TEXT- GE Q2 rises 14 pct to $0.66 shr.

text.p: GE Quarterly Earnings Highest in Company's History; Earnings Per Share Up 14% to Record $.66; Operating Margin Reaches Record Level of 17.1%

FAIRFIELD, Conn., July 10 /PRNewswire/ -- GE's second-quarter earnings of $2.162 billion were the highest for any quarter in the Company's history, Chairman John F. Welch reported today. "The quarter's double-digit increase again demonstrates the ability of GE's diverse mix of leading global businesses to deliver top-line growth, increased margins and strong cash generation. These strong second-quarter results position GE to deliver another year of record performance in 1997," Welch said.
Specific highlights include:

-- Second-quarter earnings per share increased 14% to $.66, up from last year's $.58, and earnings increased 13% to $2.162 billion. Both earnings per share and earnings were records for the quarter. Earnings per share grew faster than earnings, reflecting the impact of shares repurchased under a four-year, $13 billion share repurchase program initiated in December 1994.

-- Second-quarter revenues, including acquisitions, rose 15% to a record $22.0 billion. Increased global activities and higher sales of spare parts and services by GE's equipment businesses were key contributors to the increase.

-- GE's second-quarter operating margin increased to a record 17.1% of sales, up from last year's 16.3%. The second-quarter increase was the sixteenth consecutive quarterly increase of GE's operating margin rate and reflected GE's ongoing emphasis on productivity and benefits from its Six Sigma quality initiative.
-- Ten of GE's twelve businesses reported higher operating profit for the second-quarter, with nine - led by GE Capital Services, NBC and Aircraft Engines - achieving double-digit increases.

-- GE Capital Services' earnings were $798 million, 17% more than last year's $683 million, benefiting from the globalization and diversity of GECS' 27 businesses. The record results were led by strong double-digit increases in its Specialty Insurance, Equipment Management and Mid-Market Financing activities.

-- Cash generated from GE's operating activities during the first half was a strong $3.5 billion, equaling last year's record level but up sharply excluding several large unusual receipts in 1996. As part of the $13 billion share repurchase program, GE purchased $862 million of its stock during the second quarter to reach $8.1 billion - 218 million shares - purchased since December 1994.
"In addition to delivering record performance for the second quarter, GE's businesses made aggressive moves to position GE for strong future growth," Mr. Welch said.
Highlights of recent activities include:
-- GE and its unions completed negotiations last week on new three-year contracts covering 38,000 GE employees which was ratified by IUE and UE members yesterday.

-- NBC won its tenth consecutive ratings sweeps victory. NBC programs took the top seven places in ratings and the network was number one in all key demographic categories. NBC broadened its cable interests by obtaining a position in Rainbow Programming Holdings - which owns eight regional sports channels, Madison Square Garden and the New York Knicks and Rangers.

-- Aircraft Engines continued its strong performance by winning more than 70% of the orders for large commercial engines during 1997. During the second quarter, the business also won several large multi-year engine service agreements, including a 10-year, $1.6 billion award from Southwest Airlines.

-- GE Capital Services continued its growth outside the United States with 11 acquisitions in Austria, Brazil, the Czech Republic, the Netherlands, Portugal and the United Kingdom. GECS also expanded its consumer savings and insurance activities with last week's announcement to acquire Colonial Penn - a direct marketer of personal auto insurance.
-- Power Systems continued its services growth with three additional multi-year power plant service agreements, pushing the value of its 1997 service awards over the $1 billion mark.
-- Plastics formed a new joint venture with Bayer AG of Germany to focus on polycarbonate automotive windows.
-- Appliances introduced a new premium appliance product line - Profile Performance - and launched a line of water filtration and softening products.
"At the halfway point in the year," Welch concluded, "GE is on track to deliver record results to its shareowners in 1997."
GENERAL ELECTRIC COMPANY
All amounts except per share earnings and average shares are in millions of U.S. dollars and reflect the two-for-one stock split effective April 28, 1997.
